Question:
An equilateral triangle is placed inside a larger equilateral triangle so that the region between them can be divided into three congruent trapezoids, as shown below. The side length of the inner triangle is \(\frac{2}{3}\) the side length of the larger triangle. What is the ratio of the area of one trapezoid to the area of the inner triangle?

[Figure 1](figures/2023_AMC_8_Q19_question_fig1.svg)
Solution:
The two equilateral triangles have the same shape. When all lengths are multiplied by \(\frac23\), both the base and the height are multiplied by \(\frac23\), so the area is multiplied by \(\left(\frac23\right)^2=\frac49\).

We may therefore measure the outer triangle's area as \(9\) units and the inner triangle's area as \(4\) units. The region between them has area \(9-4=5\) units. Since its three trapezoids are congruent, each has area \(\frac53\) units.

The requested ratio is

\[
\frac53:4=\boxed{5:12},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). Similar figures let us compare areas without finding any actual side lengths, but we must square the length ratio.
